observations.body: Egypt has thick darkness for three days; people do not see one another or rise from their places.
observations.label: Three days

observations.body: The children of Israel have light in their dwellings while darkness covers Egypt.
observations.label: Light in the dwellings

observations.body: Pharaoh permits people and children to leave but tells Moses to leave flocks and herds behind.
observations.label: A limited departure

observations.body: Moses says the livestock must go because the people do not yet know what they will use in service.
observations.label: Not a hoof

observations.body: Pharaoh threatens death if Moses sees his face again, and Moses says that he will not see it again.
observations.label: Faces and death

payload.posture: Notice the three-day darkness, Israel’s light, the proposed limits on departure, and the closing words between Pharaoh and Moses.
payload.tension: Pharaoh’s permission to leave still retains the animals Moses says are needed for service, and the exchange ends with a threat and a final word about seeing one another again.
payload.title: Light, darkness, and what may leave
